A1.justification: The PDFs clearly describe successive versions of the same event-based flow/stereo framework, and all supplied pages are readable. However, v1 references an appendix and v2 references supplementary material that neither supplied PDF contains, limiting comparison of those additional details and results.

before.justification: v1 reports original DSEC experiments, including single-task and unified-model results, cross-task transfer experiments, and component ablations in Tables 1–7.

after.justification: v2 reports original DSEC results, component ablations, feature visualizations, training curves, and qualitative generalization experiments in Tables 1–4 and Figures 5–9.

M1.justification: v2 replaces the shared ResNet encoder with a Temporal Recurrent Network processing voxel groups through residual blocks and ConvGRUs, with a top-down feature pyramid. Flow supervision changes from L1 to L2, loss weighting from 0.7 to 0.8, and flow refinement from six to three iterations. The six-stage self-/cross-attention stack largely persists under the SCA name.

E1.justification: DSEC remains the evaluated dataset, with optical flow and stereo matching retained. v2 Section 4.4 and Figure 9 add sparse-input scenarios using one-tenth the accumulation duration and one-sixteenth the event count. These extend input-condition coverage without introducing another dataset or prediction task.

E2.justification: v2 adds ECDDP to the flow comparison and ETAM-TSCLM and TESNet to stereo, while dropping v1's explicitly no-history E-RAFT* and IDNet* comparison rows. The unified-model comparison also adds IDNet and TESNet. Qualitative comparisons replace E-RAFT with IDNet and add TESNet. Concentration Net and Se-cff are the same retained baseline, as confirmed by their cited work.

E3.justification: v1 reports 600k flow, 800k stereo, and 600k joint-training iterations with a maximum learning rate of 1e-4. v2 reports 400k iterations at 3e-4 with batch size four, followed by 150k full-resolution iterations at 1e-5 with batch size one. Voxel bins increase from five to fifteen. Ablations change to a scaled-down joint model trained for 200k plus 10k iterations.

E4.justification: v1's coarse module ablations are replaced by joint-model tests separating TRN/ConvGRU and SCA/attention/FFN/positional encoding, while the propagation ablation is no longer shown. v2 additionally investigates feature-space alignment using PCA, examines sampling-induced distribution shifts, and extends transfer analysis with training curves and single/cross/unified qualitative comparisons.

E5.justification: Neither supplied PDF reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, error bars, or statistical significance tests. v2 Figure 7 shows convergence over training iterations rather than uncertainty estimates.

E6.justification: Proposed-model results are extensively replaced under changed architecture and training conditions. v1 reports unified EPE/MAE of 0.75/0.54 in Table 3; v2 reports 0.64/0.47 in Table 1. Single-task results change from 0.736/0.519 to 0.67/0.49. v2 also reports new final cross-task results and revised ablation and robustness findings. These are not controlled same-setting gains; rounding of retained baseline scores is not counted.

T1.justification: v1 Section 3 derives camera-projection, motion, and stereo-disparity relationships, including an approximately constant-disparity assumption during event accumulation. This derivation is absent from the supplied v2, which instead presents a general feature-warping objective and separate flow/stereo formulations. The formal stereo-matching objective also changes from squared feature differences to an L1 norm.

C1.justification: The overarching unification, transfer, and state-of-the-art claims remain. However, v2 replaces the explicitly claimed geometric-analysis contribution with TRN and SCA as its central technical contributions, emphasizing temporal/spatial feature aggregation. Its conclusion also introduces claims of reduced deployment complexity and resource demands. This substantially revises the claimed contribution beyond renaming EventMatch to EMatch.

C2.justification: v2 introduces a central explanation that direct voxel encoding wastes temporal structure, motivating recurrent aggregation, and develops the role of contextual attention at locations without events. Sections 4.1 and 4.4 newly attribute joint-model performance and sparse-input generalization to more diverse temporal/spatial training distributions. These extend v1's interpretation of matching, refinement, and transfer convergence.

D1.justification: v2 newly specifies 100 ms event windows, crop/full-image sizes, spatial augmentation, flipping probabilities, and ablation parameter counts; hardware changes from RTX 4090 to RTX 3090. Conversely, v1's AdamW weight decay/betas/epsilon, local matching-window sizes, and five-iteration task-switch cadence are omitted. Code remains promised rather than supplied, with v2 specifying release upon acceptance.

R1.justification: Section 2 substantially revises positioning around shared correspondence matching versus task-specific regression. v2 expands discussion of joint flow/stereo research with works including SENSE, UNOS, GeoNet, and DF-Net, and explicitly distinguishes its approach from TESNet's flow-guided stereo training. v1's Perceiver IO and unified contrast-maximization discussion is displaced. These are substantive positioning changes beyond citation renumbering.

P1.justification: v2 extensively rewrites the abstract, introduction, related work, and method narrative. It combines the previous formulation and method sections, promotes multi-task training before cross-task analysis, and introduces dedicated ablation and generalization subsections. The title, model terminology, and author list also change.

P2.justification: v2 adopts a two-column layout and redraws the overview, geometric illustration, and architecture diagrams. It adds a TRN schematic, PCA visualization, convergence plots, and robustness figure; reorganizes qualitative comparisons; and merges task-specific ablations into a joint table with parameter counts. These are extensive display changes, beyond renumbering or numerical updates.

improvement.justification: v2 substantially strengthens the empirical justification for shared event representations. Compared with v1's coarse ablations and mainly qualitative account of joint-training benefits, it separately tests temporal recurrence and attention components, reports stronger comparisons among training modes, and examines sparse-input behavior against relevant competitors. These additions make the central mechanism and its benefits more assessable. They outweigh the loss of geometric derivation and some implementation detail, although robustness remains qualitative, supplementary material is unavailable, and changed training conditions prevent attributing cross-version gains to individual components.
